newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Madame Tussaud's wax exhibit to tour Asia.
newsitem.headline: Madame Tussaud's wax exhibit to tour Asia.

text.p: London's famous Madame Tussaud's wax museum will make a rare foray outside Europe when it brings many of its wax figures to Asia later this year.
Over 100 statues in wax, representing some of the world's best-known figures of history and contemporary life, will tour Australia and Southeast Asia, starting in Melbourne in October.
Some local celebrities have been added to the Australian exhibition, nearly all of them sporting personalities, including cricketer Shane Warne, the Victoria state government said.
Marie Tussaud began her work as a modeller in wax in post-revolutionary France and founded the waxworks exhibition of famous people in London. She died in 1850
Madame Tussaud's wax museum, owned by media group Pearson Plc, draws about 2.5 million visitors each year.
